  5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS (5) Minutes

minutes_text:
MINUTES
  MEETING OF THE GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION

  COUNCIL CHAMBER, City Hall – 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206

  May 6, 2019
  4:00 PM

1. ROLL CALL
  Present: President Avanessian, Commissioners Carrasco, Kedikian, and Lall
  Absent: Commissioner Watson

2. CONSENT ITEMS
  a. Approval of the March 3, 2019 Meeting Minutes
  Motion to Approve:
  Moved by: Commissioner Kedikian
  Seconded by: Commissioner Lall
  Motion Passed.

3. REPORTS – INFORMATION
  a. Customer Services Update. Tami Vallier, Customer Services Administrator, presented an overview of the Customer
  Service Department and reported on customer service metrics. She explained Customer Services’ sections and the
  functions of each of them; provided an overview on how customers contact GWP and why; presented goals and statistics
  regarding calls and phone services; and discussed trends in payment. Ms. Vallier described the billing and collections
  process and new procedures that will be going into effect for delinquent water bills due to SB 998. Ms. Vallier presented
  recent accomplishments and described current projects. She responded to the Commissioner’s questions regarding
  procedures for identity theft, payment arrangements, rates of disconnection, and the Glendale Care program.

  b. Electric Load Shedding Protocol/ Curtailment.
  Mark Young, Integrated Resources Planning Administrator, gave a general overview of GWP’s load shedding procedures
  for manual load shedding and under-frequency load shedding (UFLS). Load and generation need to be matched each
  second. Mr. Young stated that if they are out of balance, and if balance cannot be achieved with GWP’s generation
  resources, then load will need to be curtailed. Prior to a load shedding event, GWP would reach out to LADWP for
  emergency assistance, but if LADWP cannot provide emergency assistance, GWP would need to engage in load
  shedding. GWP would rotate the load shedding among different feeders. Relative to other utilities, GWP has a higher
  number of customers on each feeder, and a feeder can serve a mix of commercial and residential users. Seventeen
  percent of facilities in the City are designated as critical facilities and would not be touched in response to a manual load
  shedding. In response to a question from Commissioner Kedikian, Mr. Young stated that the public is not notified in
  advance of manual load shedding or UFLS events as they are for a heat alert or a demand response event, because
  manual load shedding and UFLS occur very quickly; it is an emergency situation. Mr. Zurn added that there are
  restrictions on our ability to notify customers electronically. In response to a question from Commissioner Lall, Mr. Young
  stated that GWP has never had a load shedding event in his experience, but as Grayson becomes older and less reliable,
  the possibility becomes greater. Mr. Zurn stated that we have had some close calls. He noted that this summer will be
  the most difficult yet with the state of Grayson, and we do have to plan for the possibility of load shedding.
 4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS (Starting at 57:28)
  Glenn T. Webb presented a zero carbon resource plan.

5. AGENDA FORECAST
  The Commissioners and Mr. Zurn discussed the following agenda for the June 3, 2019 meeting:
   Utility Modernization Update
   Budget Presentation
   Strategic Plan
   Legislative Update

  Mr. Zurn stated that staff will schedule a special meeting, hopefully in June, to discuss the Clean Energy RFP and the Integrated
  Resources Plan. GWP staff will identify possible meeting dates with those members of the Commission that do not have a
  conflict of interest.

  Commissioner Lall suggested that GWP staff confirm whether there is a quorum for the July 1, 2019 meeting due to the holiday.

  Commissioner Lall requested a presentation at a future meeting regarding transmission, and Commissioner Carrasco agreed.
  Mr. Zurn stated that the issue will be discussed with the focus group that was convened for the IRP and with Council, and
  transmission will generally be covered in the GWP Commission special meeting regarding the IRP, but a more specific
  discussion of transmission will be scheduled for a regular GWP Commission meeting in the future.

6. ADJOURNMENT
  Motion to Adjourn:
  Moved by: Commissioner Kedikian
  Seconded by: Commissioner Carrasco
  Motion Passed.
  The meeting was adjourned at 5:50 pm.
